Break ties by tail, A to Z, so the panel doesn't reshuffle every time it refreshes.
A query starts with from, then latest, join, where, group by, compute, sort, limit, and select last. Each runs on what the one before produced, and a clause out of order is an error.
Compare with ==; a single = only names a column in compute and select. Strings take double quotes; single quotes are an error.
Every comparison with a missing value is false, != included, so status != "x" leaves out rows with no status. Test for it with is missing or is not missing. In Python, missing is None.
count(*) counts the rows in the group; count(x) counts the rows where x isn't missing. sum, avg, min, and max skip missing values, and give missing if the group has none.
After group by, the rows are the groups: only the group keys and the computed columns are left. A missing key makes its own group, and groups come out in no particular order.

topic: Rows with no match in a join
answer: A plain join keeps every row, matched or not: a row with no match keeps going, with the other table's columns missing. join inner keeps only the rows that match.
If the joined table has a column with the same name as one you already have, other than the on column, it comes back prefixed with its table's name: aircraft.status.
latest per key by column keeps each key's row with the largest value of that column. It comes right after from, so it runs before where.
$name stands for a value you pass in params. Parameters are values only, never a column or table name, and a parameter with no value is an error. limit takes one too.

sort col desc, other sorts by col, largest first, then other. Missing values always sort last, either way. limit runs after sort. select is last: it picks and names the columns, so earlier clauses can't use its names.
hours_between(start, end) gives the hours between two ISO times, round(x, digits) rounds, and lower lowercases. Each gives missing for a missing argument, and they work around aggregates in compute.
Anything wrong with a query raises weft.QueryError, with what's wrong and the line and column.
Every time in the warehouse is UTC, as ISO text, so the hours between departure and arrival are the real flying time, even between Portland and Boise.
